q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis of NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance

## (a) Time left until resolution

The earnings release is scheduled for August 26, 2026 (tomorrow, as of today being August 25, 2026). This means resolution occurs in approximately **1 day**.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

NVIDIA has already provided official guidance of **$91.0 billion ± 2%** ($89.2B–$92.8B range), issued on May 20, 2026. This is not a forecast—it is the company's own forward guidance that has already been publicly committed.

The earnings release tomorrow will formally reaffirm, narrow, or revise this guidance. Given:
- The guidance was issued only ~3 months ago (May 20 to August 26)
- Wall Street consensus ($91.8B–$91.9B) falls squarely within the existing guidance range
- There is no indication of major supply/demand disruptions in the interim
- Companies typically maintain guidance unless material changes have occurred

The **most likely outcome is that NVIDIA will reaffirm guidance near the midpoint of $91.0B**, possibly with slight adjustments but almost certainly within or very close to the existing $89.2B–$92.8B band.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Unexpected weakness in data center demand signals
- Supply chain disruptions not previously disclosed
- Macro deterioration affecting enterprise capex spending
- Geopolitical developments (e.g., expanded China export restrictions)
- Lower-than-expected GPU pricing or ASP pressure
- Customer inventory corrections

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Accelerated AI infrastructure spending by cloud providers
- Better-than-expected demand from new customer cohorts
- Pricing power stronger than anticipated
- Upside surprise from emerging applications or use cases
- Resolution of supply constraints ahead of schedule

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

From the research provided:
- NVIDIA's official guidance: **$91.0 billion ± 2%** = $89.2B–$92.8B range
- Wall Street consensus: $91.8B–$91.9B (within guidance)
- Zacks consensus: $91.8B (within guidance)

No reliable historical base rate for guidance revision magnitude is provided in the materials. However, the convergence of all three measures (company guidance midpoint, Yahoo consensus, Zacks) around $91–$92B strongly suggests this is the consensus expectation for forward guidance.

---

## Reasoning on distribution

Given that:
1. The company has already committed to formal guidance ($91.0B ± 2%)
2. We are only 1 day away from the announcement
3. Wall Street is already aligned with guidance
4. No major catalysts or disruptions have been reported in the interim

The forward guidance announcement will almost certainly cluster tightly around the existing guidance range. A reasonable distribution centered on the midpoint of current guidance ($91.0B) with modest tail risk in both directions:

- **10th percentile (lower tail):** Modest downward revision to ~$89.5B (accounting for conservative management and potential macro softness)
- **50th percentile (median):** Reaffirmation or slight upward adjustment to ~$91.0B–$91.5B
- **90th percentile (upper tail):** Upward revision to ~$93.0B (accounting for AI momentum, supply confidence, pricing strength)

The range provided ($99.5B–$115.5B) extends well beyond historical guidance patterns and would require material surprises or a major strategic shift. I will anchor my distribution within the more empirically grounded $89–$94B band based on disclosed guidance.

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA is scheduled to release its Q2 FY2027 earnings on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, after the US market close, with the analyst call at 2 p.m. PT [piptheory.com](https://piptheory.com/research/nvidia-q2-fy2027-earnings-preview-august-2026). The company's own guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, issued on May 20, 2026, is $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027). This creates a guidance range of approximately $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

Wall Street analysts, according to Yahoo! Finance, have an average estimate near $91.9 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), while Zacks consensus sits at $91.8 billion [piptheory.com](https://piptheory.com/research/nvidia-q2-fy2027-earnings-preview-august-2026). Both consensus figures are within NVIDIA's guided range, implying analysts are projecting a modest beat that the company's outlook already contains [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). NVIDIA's outlook explicitly assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027).
